summary: Pierce County 100-ft wooden tower (1955) abandoned since 1970 on Joint Base Lewis-McChord; still standing and fenced; visits need a base permit when the area is open.

facts.status_note: Abandoned since 1970 but still standing on Joint Base Lewis-McChord; fenced. NHLR says it has been threatened with demolition in recent years.

access.note: Inside JBLM Training Area 4, open for recreation only part of the time; a visitor permit and range pass are required. NHLR says access is restricted but possible by contacting the base.

visit.trail_note: Fenced and not safe to climb (WillhiteWeb). TrailChick describes reaching it from the base's east gate when the training area is open.

facts.agency: Department of Natural Resources - Washington State Division of Forestry (per NHLR); the land is Joint Base Lewis-McChord

events.note: Abandoned; no later staffing recorded in these sources
An effort was made to save the tower; the Army was considering using it for demolition practice; the tower was later offered for sale with conditions for removal. Outcome not found.

corrections.why: NHLR and TrailChick both describe a 100-foot wooden tower, about 30.5 m. No source supports 2.4 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 541 ft (165 m), which matches the brief's 164.9 m. TrailChick and a blog post both give 480 ft. Not resolved; the story notes the disagreement.
NHLR says abandoned since 1970 and threatened with demolition; WillhiteWeb says still standing and fenced. Both agree the tower stands. The most recent dated source found is the 2022 NHLR listing.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 2.4 is wrong for a 100-ft tower; corrected to 30.5. The elevation disagreement (541 ft NHLR vs 480 ft TrailChick and a blog) is unresolved. No source explains why or by whom the tower was built, and the outcome of the 2002 sale is unknown. Access depends on JBLM Training Area 4 schedules and a Range Control permit, which I did not verify with the base. The substack post is undated and was used only for access and elevation.
